coverage.priority: Germany materially deeper than wider Europe; rank by technical fit rather than geography
coverage.sourceCoveragePrinciple: Germany-first broad discovery across official employer/ATS sources, public employment and research portals, universities, research institutes, MedTech ecosystem sources, notified-body/recruiter channels and reputable aggregators. Wider Europe is included only when a role clears the same strict candidate-fit and current/open verification gates.
mandatorySourceLayers: notified/conformity-assessment bodies including TÜV SÜD, TÜV Rheinland, DEKRA and DQS Medizinprodukte
coverage.searchMethod: Daily incremental past-24h/past-week discovery plus periodic broad recall; official-source verification before publication; strict 0-years gate; technical/CV fit; language and country-specific work-authorization assessment; separate sponsorship/relocation signals; vacancy-fingerprint deduplication; material-change detection; false-negative hunt.
coverage.acceptanceAssessment: PASS. Germany remains the primary coverage layer. Three genuinely new Europe/Germany opportunities cleared the 75% publication threshold after official-source verification. Existing qualifying roles were rechecked where current sources were available. The Bosch NV-diamond role was re-evaluated and removed from active publication because its official profile requires deep quantum-physics/microwave expertise and very good German, creating a material candidate-fit failure. Multiple new Bosch/TH Mannheim/Stryker opportunities were screened but excluded below the threshold or for material skill/language/student-status gaps.
limitations: A 75% score is a modelled CV-fit assessment, not a hiring guarantee
No single run can guarantee 100% recall across every European vacancy
Some employer ATS pages expose limited metadata to search engines
Work authorization for non-Germany roles must be checked separately before accepting an offer
Discovery-board results are signals only and are not used as final evidence
The candidate's B1 German materially reduces eligibility for roles requiring B2/C1 German
